title: FA/80/2011 of RAMPAL SINGH Vs SMT PUNAM

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Appeal No.80 of 2011
Rampal Singh ....Appellant
Versus
Smt. Punam .... Respondent

Present: Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the respondent.
Date: 16th June 2015
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.

Present first appeal has been filed by the husband
(appellant) for setting aside the judgment and order dated
18.07.2011 passed by learned Judge Family Court, Pauri Garhwal
in Case No.115 of 2008, Rampal vs. Smt. Punam and to grant a
decree of divorce in favour of the appellant dissolving his marriage
with the respondent (wife).
2. A suit was filed by husband against his wife under
Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act for the purpose of getting decree
of dissolution of marriage on the basis of cruelty and discretion.
3. Defendant (respondent herein) filed her written
statement (replies), admitted her marriage with the plaintiff
(appellant herein). She stated that after the marriage, plaintiff
started saying that parents of the plaintiff were against their
marriage. After one month of marriage, when father of defendant
came to bring back defendant, the mother of plaintiff had abused
defendant and misbehaved with the father of defendant. Plaintiff
send defendant with her father and did not come to bring back for
four months. At the time of pregnancy, plaintiff forcefully left
defendant at her father's house in January, 2001. Defendant gave
birth to a son on 26th January, 2001. Plaintiff brought back
defendant on 8th February, 2001 at Kotdwar. Christening ceremony

2
of the son was performed on 9th February, 2001 and on this
occasion also all work of the house was done by defendant. Mother
of plaintiff exhorted others for giving poison to the defendant,
whenever an opportunity so arises. On 4th April, 2002 defendant
and her son were suffering from viral fever, therefore, parents of
defendant came to defendant's matrimonial home. Mother of
plaintiff used filthy abusing languages to the parents of the
defendant and assaulted her. In April, 2002 plaintiff send defendant
to her parental house and told that he will get the Government
quarter very soon and then he would bring defendant with him.
Even after getting Government quarter at B.E.L., plaintiff did not
bring defendant back. Instead, he sent a notice to the defendant
through his Advocate on 28th November, 2002 with various
allegations. It was written that if defendant did not want to live with
plaintiff, plaintiff will proceed for dissolution of marriage against
defendant. On 9th December, 2002 defendant send reply to the
notice stating therein that she was ready to live with to plaintiff and
he may come to take defendant. Even after that, plaintiff did not
come to take defendant back.
4. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, the following
points for determination were framed:-
1. Whether defendant deserted plaintiff without
 any reason in April, 2004?
2. Relief to what the plaintiff is entitled.
3. Whether the defendant behaved plaintiff with
 cruelty? if so, its effect?

5. Learned counsel for the parties adduced oral and
documentary evidence in support of their cases. Learned Court
below came to the conclusion that after solemnization of the
marriage of the parties on 23.04.2000 till February, 2002, the
plaintiff did not allege cruelty against the defendant. The Court
below has elaborately dealt with the evidence of the parties and

3
reached to a finding that the plaintiff has failed to prove the
allegation of cruelty against defendant. Plaintiff himself did not
object defendant's going to her parents' home. He himself went
with the defendant to drop her at her parental house at Najibabad
till 2004. In that situation, it was not permissible to plaintiff to have
taken a plea that the defendant visited her parental home quite
frequently and thereby treated the plaintiff with cruelty.
6. So far as the issue of the desertion is concerned,
learned court below held, after discussing the rival contentions, and
banking upon relevant decisions of the hon'ble superior courts on
the point, that the plaintiff (husband) has failed to prove desertion
against the defendant (wife). Based upon such findings, the
Principal Judge, Family Court, Pauri Garhwal dismissed the suit of
the husband for dissolution of marriage against defendant under
Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
7. After considering the rival submissions and having
gone through the record of the case, we are of the view that learned
Judge, Family Court, has erred in holding that the appellant failed
to prove desertion. The fact remains that since April, 2004 the
respondent never visited the house of the appellant. Although she
stated that on four occasions, the appellant visited her, but this fact
has been specifically denied by the husband (appellant). The court
below reached to the conclusion that appellant might have visited
her house is purely based upon the conjectures and surmises. Thus,
in our view the wife (respondent) deserted husband (appellant) for
more than two years. On this ground alone, we allow the appeal and
set aside the judgment and decree dated 18.07.2011. The marriage
between appellant-husband and respondent-wife is dissolved and
the decree of divorce is granted.

4
8. On the basis of interaction with the parties and their
counsels, we are able to reach to the following conclusion, which is
based upon amicable settlement between the parties. :-
9. As far as the issue of son Pranjal is concerned, we find
that he is minor. Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Advocate for the appellant
made statement that appellant is ready to pay `5,00,000/-(Rupees
Five Lacs) as maintenance allowance for his son and he will pay
the same in the name of his son and respondent, which may be kept
in a fixed deposit and should be used for the purpose of studies of
the child only. Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the respondent also
submits that respondent is agreeable to this proposal and she does
not want anything for herself. She only wants that future of her son
should be saved. We record the statements of learned counsel for
the parties and direct the appellant to handover the draft of
`5,00,000/-(Rupees Five Lacs) to the respondent. The draft shall be
prepared in the joint name of Smt. Punam and Pranjal. The amount
shall be paid to the child after he attains majority. The amount can
also be encashed earlier, if same is required for higher studies of
her son. In case, bank draft is to be encashed before Pranjal attains
the age of majority, in that event the bank Manager of concerned
bank shall also verify this fact. We also direct the respondent to
permit the appellant to visit his son once in a month.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.) (V.K. Bist, J.)
 16.06.2015 16.06.2015
